guideposts.label: Welcome to Almeria
guideposts.detail: Today’s stage is entirely set in the province of Almeria, visited by La Vuelta for the first time since Kaden Groves won in Cabo de Gata in 2022. Cristian Rodríguez (XDS Astana) is the local rider of the day as he hails from El Ejido, near Almeria, around 100 kilometres from today’s course. The main local cycling event is the Clasica de Almeria, held since 1986 and won by Biniam Girmay last Februa

guideposts.label: An unprecedented start… where Hayter already built sweet memories
guideposts.detail: Vera make its debut as La Vuelta stage town*. Ethan Hayter won the final stage of the 2021 Vuelta a Andalucia, starting in Vera. *The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio

guideposts.label: Brennan in the footsteps of Pogacar, Gaviria and Sagan
guideposts.detail: A few weeks after his 21st birthday, Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) already has three Grand Tour stage wins under his belt. He is the first Grand Tour debutant with three stage wins since Tadej Pogacar in La Vuelta 19. He is the first sprinter to claim three stage wins in his maiden Grand Tour since Fernando Gaviria in the Giro 2017. The Colombian even pushed his tally to four wins on that o

guideposts.label: 3 non-starters
guideposts.detail: There are 163 riders in the absence of Ben Tulett (Visma-Lease a Bike), David Gonzalez (Pinarello Q36.5) and Lindsay De Vylder (Alpecin-Premier Tech).

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Alessandro Romele (8th), Henok Mulubrhan (13th) and Harold Tejada (24th) in the mix yesterday, XDS Astana had the best collective performance in Lorca, but Decathlon CMA CGM retained the lead of the overall team standings ahead of Netcompany Ineos (42’’55’’) and Visma-Lease a Bike (50’12’’).

guideposts.label: An intense start
guideposts.detail: Many attackers try their chance, with Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) and EF Education-EasyPost riders proving particularly intent on making the break. Frederik Wandahl (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) crashed but he got back on his bike. The bunch is packed at km 6.

guideposts.label: On the first climb of the day
Dunbar is the first to bridge the gap
guideposts.detail: A dozen more chasers join the attackers, starting with Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates), but the peloton are right behind.

guideposts.label: Van Aert and Buitrago keep pushing on the downhill
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Santiago Butirago (Bahrain Victorious) are a few metres ahead at km 19. The peloton has split.

guideposts.label: The attackers are caught at km 20
guideposts.detail: Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) launches a new move.

guideposts.label: McKenzie abandons
guideposts.detail: Hamish McKenzie (Jayco AlUla) suffered a hard crash yesterday.

guideposts.label: 3 attackers with a small gap
guideposts.detail: Axel Laurance (Netcompany Ineos), Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and Alexey Lutsenko (NSN) are 17 seconds ahead of the bunch after 25 kilometres of racing.

guideposts.label: A gap of 12'' after 35 km
guideposts.detail: The chasers have been reeled in. Attacks keep flying.

guideposts.label: Onley is chasing behind the peloton after a crash
guideposts.detail: The white jersey wearer went down in a roundabout and rapidly resumed racing.

guideposts.label: The breakaway
46.8 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: It was an impressive battle for the attackers to get away. And it keeps going with three chasers in pursuit: Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG), José Manuel Diaz Gallego (Burgos-Burpellet BH) and Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL). The peloton trail by 2'45''.

guideposts.label: Wout van Aert (Visma | Lease a Bike)
2 more riders in the breakaway
guideposts.detail: José Manuel Diaz Gallego (Burgos-Burpellet BH) and Chris Hamilton (Picnic PostNL) make it a 30-man front group. Pavel Sivakov (UAE Emirates XRG) trails by 45 seconds.

guideposts.label: More movement in the breakaway
guideposts.detail: Almeida, Van Aert, Bisiaux, Buitrago, Lutsenko and Kron attack ahead of the third climb of the day, but their breakaway rivals react.

guideposts.label: 100 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The thirty leaders get back together. The last gap to the bunch: 5'10''.

guideposts.label: The breakaway
La Vuelta stage winners in the breakaway
guideposts.detail: Three years ago today, on 3 September 2023, Lennard Kamna (Lidl-Trek) won at Collado de la Cruz de Caravaca a stage that started in Cartagena (yesterday's start town). The other stage winners in the breakaway are: - Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) : Castelo Branco 2024, Cordoba 2024, Baiona 2024 - Pablo Castrillo (Movistar) : Estacion de Montana de Manzaneda 2024, Valgrande-Pajares.Cuitu Negru

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 39.1 km/h
guideposts.detail: The leaders maintain a strong pace and keep extending their lead: 5'57''.

guideposts.label: Van Aert also takes the 3rd summit of the day
guideposts.detail: Buitrago tried to anticipate, but he was second again.

guideposts.label: The gap has increased on the climb
guideposts.detail: The peloton crest the ascent with the biggest gap so far today: 6'35''.

guideposts.label: The attackers are back on the valley
guideposts.detail: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious) are caught after opening a gap of 20 seconds on the downhill.

guideposts.label: Memories from Alto de Velefique and Calar Alto
guideposts.detail: Alto de Velefique was introduced in La Vuelta 2004, en route to the first summit finish at Calar Alto. It has been passed in every stage finishing at Calar Alto (2004, 2006, 2017) and was also the setting of two summit finishes in 2009 and 2021. On the last occasion, Damiano Caruso took the stage winter a 71-km solo attack. Wearing La Roja, Primoz Roglic was second at the summit ahead of Enric Mas

guideposts.label: Santiago Buitrago (Bahrain Victorious)
De la Cruz: "Calar Alto is a very uneven climb"
guideposts.detail: David de la Cruz (Pinarello-Q36.5) was 10th at Calar Alto in 2017 and he described the challenges before today’s stage: "I have bittersweet memories because, to be honest, my legs felt really strong that day but I had a mechanical problem right at the start of the climb, which meant I couldn’t fight for the win. It’s a very uneven climb. The first section is very tough; the first 5 kilometres are

guideposts.label: Omrzel stands on the virtual GC podium
guideposts.detail: The peloton reach km 104 with a gap of 6'40''. The Slovenian youngster trailed by 8'05'' at the start of the stage.

guideposts.label: 7 minutes
guideposts.detail: The attackers are working hard on the valley leading to Velefique. They will soon enter the final 50 kilometres. Pello Bilbao (Bahrain Victorious) returns to the front group after a mechanical.

guideposts.label: Carapaz attacks from far away
guideposts.detail: The Ecuadorian climber came from behind and went all in! He is about 39 km from the finish.

guideposts.label: Omrzel accelerates
guideposts.detail: Only Bisiaux follows the Slovenian into the final three kilometres up the Alto de Velefique. Tuckwell sets the pace in the chase group. He's followed by Buitrago, Berrade, Haig, Lutsenko, Garcia Pierna and Vansevenant.

guideposts.label: Arthur Kluckers abandons
guideposts.detail: Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) is the last rider from Luxembourg in the peloton after the withdrawal of Arthur Kluckers (Tudor) and Alex Kirsch (Cofidis).

guideposts.label: Carapaz is caught by the GC group
guideposts.detail: Meanwhile, the attackers are inside the final kilometre of ascent.

guideposts.label: Buitrago goes first atop the Alto de Velefique
guideposts.detail: Omrzel and Bisiaux were caught just before the summit.

guideposts.label: Results at the Alto de Velefique (cat. 1, km 135.4)
guideposts.detail: 1. Buitrago, 10 pts / 6'' 2. Lutsenko, 6 pts : 4'' 3. Tuckwell, 4 pts / 2'' 4. Haig, 2 pts 5. Bisiaux, 1 pt

guideposts.label: 20 kilometres to go for the leaders
guideposts.detail: At the same time, the GC group enter the final 25 kilometres with a gap of 5'10''.

guideposts.label: The highest summit finish of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: At 2,153 metres, Calar Alto is the highest summit finish of La Vuelta 26. Last year, stage 20 finished at 2,251 metres (Bola del Mundo). Jonas Vingegaard was the winner to seal his overall victory. Passed on stage 4 as the race headed to Andorra La Vella, Port d’Envalira (2,409m) was the other 2000+ summit of the 2026 edition. Today’s route makes for the third stage with the highest elevation gain

guideposts.label: 4 leaders with 15 km to go
guideposts.detail: Santiago Butirago still sets the pace. he's followed by Urko Berrade, Léo Bisiaux and Jakob Omrzel.

guideposts.label: Gall attacks from far away
guideposts.detail: Mas jumps on the Austrian's wheel. Roglic also follows. Onley tries to chase. Muhlberger and Carapaz follow him.

guideposts.label: Omrzel accelerates with 13 km to go
guideposts.detail: Only Berrade follows. Bisiaux tries to chase them.

Onley is chasing behind the peloton after a crash
Carapaz is caught by the GC group
Omrzel accelerates with 13 km to go
